claims.statement: The wiki-maintenance runbook page is a derived summary of docs/runbooks/wiki-maintenance.md and must carry a resource field pointing to that path.

pnpm nx wiki-plan infrastructure-as-code decomposes documentation changes since the last recorded run into slices of at most 8 pages per bundle area, offline and keyless; pnpm nx wiki-maintain infrastructure-as-code is the paid execution step and requires the key of whichever provider MCM_WIKI_PROVIDER selects (anthropic by default for local runs). At execution, consecutive same-kind slices of different areas are packed into one generator invocation of up to MAX_PAGES_PER_INVOCATION (8) pages, while the slice remains the unit of backlog and carry-forward.
The run record is stored at openwiki/.maintenance-state.json (committed, ephemeral-runner-safe) and is distinct from openwiki/.last-update.json, which belongs to the openwiki tool itself.

The planner caps refresh slices at 8 pages and creation slices at 3 pages, never mixing the two kinds in one slice; the creation cap of 3 is unverified and was calibrated under a now-fixed 4096-token bug.

A committed backlog slice that can never succeed under the current policy is dropped and reported as 'carried-forward page(s) dropped' on every plan; a failed slice does not block the next one, and the run stops only after two consecutive failures.

A slice is retried up to 3 times within one run before returning to the backlog; the working tree is snapshotted once before the first attempt so a forbidden write on attempt 1 persists through all retries.

The run budget is one 8-page generator invocation per run — a 4-minute deadline for starting work, a 30-minute worst-case invocation and a 60-minute job timeout, giving a declared effective ceiling of ≤16 pages / ~34 minutes of generation — and the guard test derives the workflow's timeout-minutes from those constants. Exit code 3 signals a clean budget stop with work outstanding, not a failure.

A slice fails on any of four conditions independent of the generator's own exit status: no concept page appeared (an index.md-only refresh counts as zero pages), the bundle became non-conformant, a written path was not permitted by openwiki/policy.yaml, or a requested page was left stale because it already existed, was not rewritten, and cites a resource whose last commit is newer than the page's generated.at-or-timestamp stamp (item #587). A failed slice returns to the committed backlog and the marker does not advance.
Remediation for any gate failure (conformance, leak, or governance) is always to fix openwiki/INSTRUCTIONS.md and re-run — the gates have no skip flag or allowlist by design.

CI waits ~15 minutes (concurrency + cancel-in-progress + an initial sleep) to cover a burst of merges, but defers no longer than 6 hours — that ceiling is derived from git commit dates because run state dies with cancellation while git state survives.
The proposal is one long-lived branch (openwiki-maintenance) with at most one open pull request, never auto-merged; closing it without merging returns work to the backlog and rolls the marker back.

When the run record and the forge disagree about an open proposal, the forge wins: the run asks the forge which proposal is open, adopts it if found, and treats a 409 on POST /pulls as 'adopt and update' rather than a fatal error, so a record that lost its pointer self-heals.
A protected passage may only live on a concept with no resource field; fingerprints are managed via the check-openwiki-governance.mjs --fingerprint command and declared in openwiki/protected.yaml.

The generator writes site-root-absolute body links (]/openwiki/…) which are dead on the forge; three layers hold the line: INSTRUCTIONS.md §6, verifySlice normalization, and okf-lint rules V14 and V15. A bundle-wide sweep is available via node scripts/wiki-maintain.mjs --normalize-links.

OpenWiki 0.5.x replaces the flat timestamp scalar with a structured generated:{by,at} event (OKF v0.2). finalizeGeneratedProvenance stamps generated on pages whose body changed and removes their timestamp in the same pass; unchanged pages keep their prior stamp, so both shapes coexist until all pages are regenerated.

The drift-check gate helper (used in V12) prefers generated.at and falls back to timestamp; a concept that cites a resource but carries neither is silently excluded from drift coverage — the gate counts and prints those pages as a warning, never a conformance violation.

mermaid and jsdom are optional peer dependencies of the OpenWiki generator; without them the generator falls back to a weaker built-in diagram check, silently rewriting failing fences to plain text fences while the run exits 0. Both packages are installed in .devcontainer/toolchain.Dockerfile and .forgejo/workflows/wiki-maintain.yml, and a guard in scripts/__tests__/wiki-maintain.guard.test.mjs asserts the two environments' lists match.

The wiki-update generation model pin moved from claude-sonnet-4-6 to claude-sonnet-5 in feature 075 (2026-09-21) purely for cost: same vendor, credential, workflow and Deep Agents caching middleware, only the id changed. Sonnet 5 lists at $2/$10 per MTok versus Sonnet 4.6's $3/$15, with cache reads at $0.20/MTok versus $0.30; generation was ~53% of a measured $74.89 model bill over the 30 days to 2026-09-20 and already ~92% cache reads, so the cached-read rate — not list input price — decided it, yielding roughly a 33% reduction (~$1.72 to ~$1.15 per run-day).

OpenWiki sends no temperature parameter to the model, which is why bumping the wiki-maintain pin to claude-sonnet-5 was safe where an equivalent bump broke the agent gateway: the gateway sent temperature unconditionally and Sonnet 5 / Opus 5 reject that parameter with HTTP 400. A model id is therefore only a drop-in for the sampling parameters the caller actually sends, and must be re-checked if OpenWiki ever starts sending them.

scripts/__tests__/wiki-maintain.guard.test.mjs asserts for the pinned generation model that the explicit OPENWIKI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS cap is set and at or above the 16384-token minimum a page-writing turn needs, that OpenWiki's own resolveAnthropicMaxOutputTokens regex still matches the pinned model id, and that the id would not resolve to @langchain/anthropic's 4096-token fallback if the explicit cap were removed. Its installed-generator assertions SKIP rather than fail when OpenWiki is absent from the global node_modules path or is not the pinned version, so a skip can misleadingly read as a pass; OPENWIKI_ROOT points them at a side install of the pinned version, and the wiki-maintain CI job fails the step when any check skips.

V12 drift detection is warn-only and deliberately excluded as an input to planSlices in scripts/wiki-maintain.mjs, which decomposes work only from paths changed since the run-record marker plus the carried-forward backlog; consequently a concept whose source changed after the marker passed it is not automatically re-planned (gap #526), and clearing the V12 list takes a hand-seeded sweep (--since <ref>, or pages placed in the run record's backlog). The prior route by which a planned page fell behind — #587, a refresh slice verifying as noChange while writing nothing for a requested page — is fixed by verifySlice failing the slice when a requested page's cited source is newer than its stamp; #525 remains the tracked drift-driven sweep, unblocked from the now-done #588.

OpenWiki 0.5.2 records Claims sidecars under openwiki/.claims/, one JSON file per page mirroring its bundle path, each holding schemaVersion, a pageVersion hash, a verification event, and a claims array whose entries carry an id, a statement, and repo:// evidence with resolver-computed version hashes; a later refresh marks a claim stale or unresolved when its evidence no longer matches or cannot be resolved, requiring the generator to confirm, revise, or retract it.

openwiki/policy.yaml has no dedicated rule for the .claims/ sidecar directory (it is permitted only by the openwiki/** catch-all as regenerate/actor:generator), and okf-lint does not read the sidecars themselves — its only contact with Claims is rule V5 validating the ISO-8601 shape of a page's verified.at front-matter field.

Which model writes the knowledge bundle is configuration resolved in ONE pure place, scripts/wiki-provider.mjs, from MCM_WIKI_PROVIDER: the anthropic row is the local default with model claude-sonnet-5, and the fireworks row is what the CI workflow sets at page concurrency 4 with model accounts/fireworks/models/deepseek-v4p1-flash. Each row lists the credential names it accepts and the chosen value is mapped to the name the generator reads only in the generator's own environment, with every other provider's key removed from it.

MCM_WIKI_PAGE_CONCURRENCY (validated 1–8, matching openwiki 0.6.0's MAX_PAGE_CONCURRENCY, default 1) and MCM_WIKI_SERVICE_TIER (Fireworks-only 'priority', which measured no speed gain at +25% price) are resolved alongside the provider; a malformed selector, tier or concurrency value THROWS rather than falling back to a default, surfacing as exit 2 before any paid call, and an empty value counts as unset.

The wiki-update Nx target names no provider, model, or page concurrency, because nx builds a target's child env as { ...process.env, ...targetEnv } and a value there would silently overwrite the calling job's choice; scripts/wiki-generate.mjs instead resolves the provider table, maps the credential, sets OPENWIKI_PAGE_CONCURRENCY, loads the usage tap through NODE_OPTIONS, and passes WIKI_RUN_MESSAGE as a single argv element with no shell.

Before the first paid slice, wiki-maintain --execute makes one minimal call to the selected model (node scripts/wiki-generate.mjs --preflight does the same by hand); a failure exits 2 with the run record untouched and reports the provider's error type only, so a withdrawn model id, a revoked key or a blocked egress host costs one token rather than a slice. The free plan path and --dry-run never invoke it.

The run-budget constants live in scripts/wiki-maintain.mjs: PAGE_BUDGET = MAX_PAGES_PER_INVOCATION = 8, TIME_BUDGET_SECONDS = 4 minutes (a deadline for STARTING work, so an invocation or retry under way is never interrupted), WORST_INVOCATION_SECONDS = 30 minutes, and a 60-minute job timeout derived from them by the guard test. Budgets are checked between slices, never inside one, which bounds the overshoot at one invocation.

Because OpenWiki reports no token usage itself, scripts/wiki-usage-tap.mjs is loaded into the generator process and records per-call counts (never content), which scripts/wiki-usage.mjs prices against the dated scripts/wiki-provider-prices.json; the per-invocation and run totals are logged and persisted as lastRunUsage in openwiki/.maintenance-state.json. An uncaptured invocation is recorded as 'not captured', never as $0, and a partial run states how many invocations are missing.

The exit-code contract is: 0 = plan produced, every attempted slice verified, or nothing to do; 1 = a slice failed verification; 2 = bad usage, an unreadable run record, a missing credential, a malformed MCM_WIKI_* value, or a failed preflight; 3 = stopped at the run budget with work outstanding, which is not a failure. A failed slice leaves the marker unadvanced while a budget stop advances it, because the remainder is in the backlog.
